the parasite requires scavenging of lipoylated proteins from host cell mitochondria for its survival in the host cell.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
lipoic acid is essential for parasite growth and development and that lipoic acids can be scavenged from host cells.
the parasite is dependent on host cell mitochondria for lipoic acid and that the parasite mitochondrion is the site for lipoylated proteins.
mitochondrial lipoic acid is essential for the development of Plasmodium berghei liver stage.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the scavenging of host cell lipoylated proteins by the parasite is essential for the successful completion of liver stage development in the mammalian host.
